decisions.reason: As a core drainage component built squarely on the firm's established engineering and installation know-how and supported with its own product page in both 2018 and 2019, it is likely to be retained and improved rather than withdrawn.
A floor-level shower drainage system matches the firm's stated strategic direction almost exactly, and the move from a mention in 2018 to its own page in 2019 suggests strengthening commitment.

This designer shower drainage product fits the firm's design-conscious bathroom drainage competence, but the reduced website prominence in 2019 indicates some risk that it could be folded into a broader range rather than remain a stand-alone offer.

A shower element with integrated slope is closely related to the firm's installation and waterproofing expertise, yet its limited website prominence suggests it may be more vulnerable if demand or differentiation proved weaker than expected.

Although somewhat broader than the bathroom niche, a backflow-protected basement floor drain still relies on the firm's drainage knowledge and was highlighted strongly at launch and on the home page in 2019, pointing to continued support.

An air-admittance valve is the furthest from the firm's main shower and floor-drainage product families and received only limited website emphasis, so the firm is less likely to learn enough from it to justify keeping it on the market.
